functionality.rationale: An incorrect identity check could reject every valid commit or allow misattributed commits to continue.

security.rationale: Untrusted attribution weakens the audit trail used to review and accept governed changes.

performance.rationale: Identity validation adds only constant-size config and commit metadata reads.

compatibility.rationale: The activation boundary must preserve older multi-contributor history while governing every new commit.

concurrency.rationale: The policy reads immutable commit metadata and does not add shared runtime state.

platform.rationale: Hook execution and Git identity formatting must behave consistently on macOS, Linux, and Windows Git environments.

persistence.rationale: Bootstrap deliberately rewrites repository-local name, email, and hooksPath configuration.

adr.rationale: This extends an existing internal commit governance policy without changing a product or cross-workstream contract.

architecture.rationale: The change affects development-time Git enforcement and does not alter runtime module boundaries.

roadmap.rationale: Commit attribution enforcement completes no product delivery milestone.
